title: Entropy Regularizing Activation: Boosting Continuous Control, Large Language Models, and Image Classification with Activation as Entropy Constraints
claim: Adding our plug-in activation to several standard baseline algorithms yields consistently higher learning curves than each unmodified baseline.
layout: 4 line-plot panels in a row, shared 'steps' x-axis, blue baseline vs red ours
description: A single horizontal strip of four line charts. Each panel pairs one baseline in blue with the same baseline plus the method (the ERA variant) in red. The baselines are SAC, TD-MPC2, FastTD3 and PPO, and the red variants are SAC-ERA, TD-MPC2-ERA, FastSAC-ERA and PPO-ERA. The x-axes are training steps, running to 3.0M, 1.0M, 100K and 3.0M. The y-axes are normalized scores from 0 to 1. In every panel the red curve rises above the blue one. The gap is large for SAC, TD-MPC2 and PPO and smaller for FastTD3. Each panel has a legend box at the top left and light dashed gridlines. The titles are cut off at the top edge. The eye goes to the red curves pulling away from the blue ones. The layout is clean and has no other annotations.
caption: ERA Boosts Large Language Models, Continuous Control and Image Classification. (a) Large Language Models: ERA consistently enhances the performance of Qwen-2.5-Math-7B on AIME'24,AIME'25 and AMC datasets. (b) Continuous Control: ERA significantly improves multiple popular RL algorithms, including SAC, PPO, TD-MPC2 and OBAC. (c) Image Classification: ERA consistently boosts the performance of ResNet-50 on ImageNet and CIFAR-10 datasets.
abstract: We propose ERA, a new paradigm that constrains the sampling entropy above given thresholds by applying specially designed activations to the outputs of models. Our approach demonstrates broad effectiveness across different domains: 1) for large language models(LLMs), boosting the AIME 2025 score for Qwen2.5-Math-7B by 37.4%; 2) for continuous control reinforcement learning agents, improving performance by more than 30% over strong baselines such as SAC on the challenging HumanoidBench; 3) for image classification, enhancing ImageNet top-1 accuracy by 0.69% for ResNet-50. These gains are achieved with a computational overhead of less than 7%. Our work validates output activation as a powerful tool for entropy control, opening a new direction for designing simpler and more robust algorithms.
